whyD: 'Productive and sustainable' echoes development policy terms, not the exact constitutional phrase.
explanationTl: Sa Article II, Section 16, ang right ng tao ay sa isang 'balanced and healthful ecology in accord with the rhythm and harmony of nature.'
hintTl: Dalawang idea ang pinagsama: balanse ng kalikasan at kalusugan ng tao.

text: How many Representatives are in the House based on population?
explanation: The House has not more than 250 members, but can be more with party-list.

text: What are the 3 main branches of the Government of the Philippines?
optionD: The Legislature, The Senate, The Supreme Court
explanation: The 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in Congress (Art VI), executive power in the President (Art VII), and judicial power in the Supreme Court and lower courts (Art VIII).
hint: Think of separation of powers: one branch makes laws, one carries them out, one interprets them.
whyA: These are institutions, not branches; the Senate is part of Congress, so the legislature is counted twice.
whyB: These are forms of government, not branches of government.
whyD: The Senate is part of the Legislature, and the executive branch is missing entirely.
explanationTl: Separation of powers: Legislative (Congress, Art VI), Executive (President, Art VII), at Judicial (Supreme Court at lower courts, Art VIII).
hintTl: Isa ang gumagawa ng batas, isa ang nagpapatupad, at isa ang nag-i-interpret.

text: The Supreme Court is composed of a Chief Justice and how many Associate Justices?
explanation: Art. VIII, Sec. 4(1) of the 1987 Constitution: the Supreme Court is composed of a Chief Justice and fourteen Associate Justices, 15 members in all.
hint: The full Court has 15 members; subtract the Chief Justice.
whyA: Twelve is too few; the Court has 15 members in total.
whyB: Thirteen would make only 14 members, one short.
whyD: Fifteen is the total membership including the Chief Justice, not the number of Associate Justices.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VIII, Sec. 4(1), ang Supreme Court ay may isang Chief Justice at fourteen Associate Justices, kaya 15 lahat.
hintTl: 15 ang buong Court; ibawas mo ang Chief Justice.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, who is the Commander-in-Chief of all armed forces of the Philippines?
optionC: Chief of Staff of the AFP
explanation: Art. VII, Sec. 18 of the 1987 Constitution makes the President the Commander-in-Chief of all armed forces of the Philippines.
hint: Civilian authority is supreme over the military; look for the highest civilian official.
whyA: The Defense Secretary is a Cabinet member under the President, not the Commander-in-Chief.
whyC: The AFP Chief of Staff is the top military officer but answers to the President.
whyD: The Senate President heads the Senate, part of the legislative branch.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 18, ang President ang Commander-in-Chief ng lahat ng armed forces ng Pilipinas.
hintTl: Mas mataas ang civilian authority kaysa military; sino ang pinakamataas na civilian official?

text: The executive power shall be vested in the _________.
explanation: Art. VII, Sec. 1 of the 1987 Constitution: the executive power shall be vested in the President of the Philippines.
hint: Executive means carrying out the laws; who heads the government?
whyB: The House of Representatives shares legislative power with the Senate (Art. VI, Sec. 1).
whyC: The Supreme Court holds judicial power (Art. VIII, Sec. 1).
whyD: Congress holds legislative power, not executive power.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 1, ang executive power ay nasa President of the Philippines.
hintTl: Executive = nagpapatupad ng batas. Sino ang head ng gobyerno?

text: The legislative power shall be vested in the _________ which shall consist of a Senate and a House of Representatives.
explanation: Art. VI, Sec. 1 of the 1987 Constitution vests legislative power in the Congress of the Philippines, which consists of a Senate and a House of Representatives (except the power reserved to the people by initiative and referendum).
hint: Look for the body with two chambers.
whyB: Batasang Pambansa was the legislature under the 1973 Constitution, not the 1987 one.
whyC: The Supreme Court holds judicial power (Art. VIII, Sec. 1).
whyD: The President holds executive power (Art. VII, Sec. 1).
explanationTl: Sa Art. VI, Sec. 1, ang legislative power ay nasa Congress of the Philippines, na binubuo ng Senate at House of Representatives.
hintTl: Hanapin ang body na may dalawang chamber.

text: The Senate shall be composed of how many senators elected at large by voters of the Philippines?
explanation: Article VI, Section 2 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the Senate is composed of 24 senators elected at large by the qualified voters of the Philippines.
hint: Think of the number of senatorial slots on a full ballot, which is twice the number elected every three years.
whyA: 21 is not in the Constitution; it may come from confusing the count with the number of members of other bodies.
whyB: 22 is a guess just under the real figure; the Constitution fixes it at 24.
whyC: 23 is one short; the Senate has 24 seats, 12 elected every three years.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 2 ng 1987 Constitution, 24 senators ang bumubuo sa Senate, at elected at large sila ng mga botante sa buong Pilipinas.
hintTl: Isipin mo kung ilan ang senador na binoboto every three years, tapos i-double mo.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, how long is the term of office of a senator?
explanation: Article VI, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution provides that the term of office of senators is six years, and no senator may serve more than two consecutive terms.
hint: A senator's term is twice as long as the term of a member of the House of Representatives.
whyA: 3 years is the term of a member of the House of Representatives (Art VI Sec 7), not a senator.
whyB: 4 years is not a term used for senators under the 1987 Constitution.
whyC: 5 years is not a constitutional term for senators; it may be confused with other fixed terms.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 4, six years ang term ng senador, at hanggang two consecutive terms lang ang pwede.
hintTl: Doble ang term ng senador kumpara sa congressman.

text: The President and Vice-President of the Philippines are elected for a term of how many years?
explanation: Under Art. VII, Sec. 4 of the 1987 Constitution, the President and Vice-President are elected for a term of six years. The President cannot be reelected.
hint: It is the same length as a senator's term.
whyA: Three years is the term of members of the House of Representatives (Art. VI, Sec. 7).
whyB: Four years is the US presidential term, not the Philippine one.
whyC: Five years is not the term of any elected national official under the 1987 Constitution.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VII, Sec. 4 ng 1987 Constitution, six years ang term ng President at Vice-President. Bawal nang ma-reelect ang President.
hintTl: Pareho ito ng term ng senador.

text: The members of the House of Representatives shall be elected for a term of _______.
explanation: Representatives serve 3-year terms.

text: The following shall be exempted from taxation except:
explanation: Article VI, Section 28 exempts churches, charitable institutions, and non-profit cemeteries from taxation, but not general lands and buildings.

text: The Congress, by a vote of ____ of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately, shall have the sole power to declare a state of war.
explanation: Article VI, Section 23(1) of the 1987 Constitution provides that Congress, by a vote of two-thirds of both Houses in joint session assembled, voting separately, has the sole power to declare the existence of a state of war.
hint: Declaring war is a grave act, so it needs a supermajority, the same fraction used to override a presidential veto.
whyB: One-half (a simple majority) is too low for an act as grave as declaring war.
whyC: Three-quarters is not used here; it is higher than what Section 23 requires.
whyD: Three-fifths is not the fraction in Section 23; the Constitution requires two-thirds.
explanationTl: Sa Article VI, Section 23(1), kailangan ng two-thirds vote ng both Houses, in joint session pero voting separately, para mag-declare ng state of war ang Congress.
hintTl: Mabigat na desisyon ang pag-declare ng war, kaya supermajority ang kailangan. Pareho ito sa fraction para ma-override ang veto ng President.

text: It states that “no person shall be deprived of life, liberty, or property without due process of law, nor any person be denied the equal protection of the laws.”
explanation: This is from Article III, the Bill of Rights.

text: What is the state policy on labor?
explanation: Article XIII emphasizes full protection to labor and promotion of full employment.

text: The national language of the Philippines is:
explanation: Article XIV, Section 6 of the 1987 Constitution states that the national language of the Philippines is Filipino, which shall be further developed and enriched on the basis of existing Philippine and other languages.
hint: The 1987 Constitution uses a name that is not tied to any single regional language.
whyA: English is an official language for communication and instruction (Art XIV Sec 7), not the national language.
whyC: Tagalog is a regional language that Filipino is largely based on, but the Constitution names Filipino, not Tagalog.
whyD: Cebuano is a major regional language, not the national language.
explanationTl: Ayon sa Article XIV, Section 6 ng 1987 Constitution, Filipino ang national language natin. Hindi Tagalog, kahit malaki ang base nito sa Tagalog.
hintTl: Yung pangalan na ginamit ng Constitution ay hindi pangalan ng isang rehiyon lang.

text: What is the term for the House Speaker?
explanation: The House Speaker serves at the pleasure of the House.

text: The main function of the Office of the Ombudsman is to:
optionA: Investigate complaints against public officials and employees
optionD: Decide questions on the constitutionality of laws
explanation: Under Art. XI, Secs. 12-13 of the 1987 Constitution, the Ombudsman acts on complaints against public officials and employees and investigates any illegal, unjust, improper or inefficient act or omission.
hint: The Ombudsman is called the 'protector of the people' against abuse in government.
whyB: Enacting laws belongs to Congress and local legislative bodies (Art. VI, Sec. 1).
whyC: Auditing government funds is the job of the Commission on Audit (Art. IX-D).
whyD: Ruling on constitutionality is a power of the Supreme Court (Art. VIII, Sec. 5).
explanationTl: Sa Art. XI, Secs. 12-13, ang Ombudsman ang nag-a-act sa complaints laban sa public officials at employees, at nag-iimbestiga ng illegal o improper na acts nila.
hintTl: Siya ang 'protector of the people' laban sa abuso sa gobyerno.

text: RA 9262 is:
explanation: RA 9262 is the Anti-VAWC Act.

text: The three major island groups of the Philippines are:
explanation: The Philippine archipelago is divided into three major island groups: Luzon in the north, the Visayas in the center, and Mindanao in the south. They are represented by the three stars on the national flag.
hint: Remember the three stars on the Philippine flag.
whyA: Palawan is a province under the Luzon group, not a separate major island group.
whyB: Sulu is an archipelago that belongs to the Mindanao group.
whyC: Samar is an island in the Visayas, not a major island group by itself.
explanationTl: Tatlo ang major island groups ng Pilipinas: Luzon sa north, Visayas sa gitna, at Mindanao sa south. Sila ang tatlong bituin sa watawat.
hintTl: Alalahanin ang tatlong bituin sa watawat ng Pilipinas.

text: Under the 1987 Constitution, Members of the Supreme Court hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of:
explanation: Art. VIII, Sec. 11 provides that Members of the Supreme Court and judges of lower courts hold office during good behavior until they reach the age of seventy years or become incapacitated.
hint: It is the same age limit that applies to judges of lower courts.
whyA: 65 is the compulsory retirement age in the general civil service, not for justices.
whyC: 75 is not the constitutional limit; justices must leave earlier.
whyD: 60 is the optional retirement age for many government workers, not the justices' limit.
explanationTl: Sa Art. VIII, Sec. 11, ang Supreme Court justices at lower court judges ay nasa pwesto habang good behavior, until mag-70 years old sila o ma-incapacitate.
hintTl: Parehong age ito para sa justices at sa mga judge ng lower courts.

text: What is the role of the Commission on Elections?
explanation: COMELEC administers elections and referenda.

text: Republic Act No. 9003 is known as the:
explanation: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000. It requires waste segregation at source and bans open dumpsites.
hint: This law is about garbage: segregation, recycling and materials recovery facilities.
whyB: The Philippine Clean Air Act is RA 8749 (1999).
whyC: The Water Code of the Philippines is PD 1067.
whyD: The Forestry Code (Revised Forestry Code) is PD 705.
explanationTl: Ang RA 9003 ay ang Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000. Dito nanggaling ang waste segregation at ang pagbabawal sa open dumpsites.
hintTl: Tungkol ito sa basura: segregation, recycling, at MRF.

text: What is the capital city of Brazil?
explanation: Brasilia is the capital city of Brazil, designed by Oscar Niemeyer and established in 1960.

text: Who was the first president of the Philippines?
explanation: Emilio Aguinaldo was the first President of the Philippines, heading the First Philippine (Malolos) Republic inaugurated in January 1899.
hint: He led the revolutionary government that declared independence in Kawit, Cavite.
whyA: Rizal was a reformist writer executed in 1896; he never held office.
whyC: Quezon was the first President of the Commonwealth (1935), not the first President.
whyD: Marcos became President only in 1965.
explanationTl: Si Emilio Aguinaldo ang first President ng Pilipinas, head ng First Philippine (Malolos) Republic na na-inaugurate noong January 1899.
hintTl: Siya ang nag-declare ng independence sa Kawit, Cavite.

text: What is the largest planet in our solar system?
explanation: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system by both mass and diameter.

text: Which gas is most abundant in Earth’s atmosphere?
explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of Earth's atmosphere by volume; oxygen is about 21%.
hint: It is not the gas we need to breathe, even though it is the one we inhale the most.
whyA: Oxygen is only about 21% of the atmosphere, second to nitrogen.
whyC: Carbon dioxide is only a tiny fraction (about 0.04%) of the atmosphere.
whyD: Argon is less than 1% of the atmosphere.
explanationTl: Mga 78% ng atmosphere ay nitrogen, habang ang oxygen ay mga 21% lang.
hintTl: Hindi ito ang gas na kailangan natin sa paghinga, pero ito ang pinakamarami sa hangin.

text: What is the national flower of the Philippines?
explanation: The sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) was proclaimed the national flower in 1934 by Governor-General Frank Murphy; it symbolizes purity and simplicity.
hint: Its small white blooms are strung into garlands sold outside churches.
whyA: Orchids such as the waling-waling are prized Philippine flowers, but the official national flower is the sampaguita.
whyC: The rose is not native and has no official status in the Philippines.
whyD: The sunflower has no official status in the Philippines.
explanationTl: Sampaguita (Jasminum sambac) ang national flower natin, idineklara noong 1934 ni Governor-General Frank Murphy. Simbolo ito ng purity at simplicity.
hintTl: Yung maliit na puting bulaklak na ginagawang kwintas at binebenta sa labas ng simbahan.

text: Which country hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics?
explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France, where Carlos Yulo won two gold medals for the Philippines.
hint: Think of where Carlos Yulo won his two gold medals.
whyB: Japan hosted the 2020 Games (held in 2021 in Tokyo).
whyC: Brazil hosted the 2016 Games in Rio de Janeiro.
whyD: Australia is set to host the 2032 Games in Brisbane.
explanationTl: Sa Paris, France ginanap ang 2024 Summer Olympics, kung saan nanalo si Carlos Yulo ng dalawang gold para sa Pilipinas.
hintTl: Saan nanalo ng dalawang gold si Carlos Yulo?

text: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
explanation: The chemical symbol for gold is Au, derived from its Latin name, aurum.

text: Which ocean is the largest in the world?
explanation: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean, covering about one-third of Earth’s surface.

text: Who wrote the novel 'Noli Me Tangere'?
explanation: Jose Rizal wrote 'Noli Me Tangere,' a novel exposing Spanish colonial abuses in the Philippines.

text: What is the longest river in the world?
explanation: The Nile River, flowing through northeastern Africa, is considered the longest river globally at about 6,650 km.

text: Which element is essential for human respiration?
explanation: Oxygen is essential for human respiration, used in cellular processes to produce energy.

text: What is the currency of Japan?
explanation: The Yen is the official currency of Japan.
hint: Its symbol is written with a Y and two bars (the same sign is used by China's currency).
whyA: The yuan is the currency of China.
whyC: The won is the currency of South Korea (and North Korea).
whyD: The ringgit is the currency of Malaysia.
explanationTl: Yen ang currency ng Japan.
hintTl: Y na may dalawang guhit ang symbol nito.

text: Which mountain is the highest in the world?
explanation: Mount Everest, in the Himalayas, is the highest mountain above sea level at 8,848 meters.

text: Who is known as the 'Father of Modern Physics'?
explanation: Albert Einstein is called the 'Father of Modern Physics' for his theory of relativity.

text: What is the national animal of the Philippines?
explanation: The Philippine Eagle is the national animal, symbolizing strength and uniqueness.

text: Which country is known as the 'Land of the Rising Sun'?
explanation: Japan is called the 'Land of the Rising Sun' due to its eastern location where the sun rises.

text: What is the primary source of energy for Earth's climate system?
explanation: Solar radiation from the Sun supplies almost all the energy that drives Earth's climate, including winds, ocean currents and the water cycle.
hint: It is also the source of daylight.
whyA: Geothermal heat is real but far too small to drive the climate.
whyC: Heat from Earth's core adds only a tiny fraction of surface energy.
whyD: Tides come from the Moon's gravity and do not power the climate.
explanationTl: Ang solar radiation galing sa Sun ang nagbibigay ng halos lahat ng energy na nagpapatakbo ng climate, kasama ang hangin, ocean currents at water cycle.
hintTl: Ito rin ang source ng liwanag sa araw.

text: Which is the largest continent by land area?
explanation: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 30% of Earth's land area. The Philippines is part of Asia.
hint: It is the continent where the Philippines is located.
whyA: Africa is the second-largest continent.
whyC: North America is the third-largest continent.
whyD: Europe is one of the smallest continents, larger only than Australia.
explanationTl: Ang Asia ang pinakamalaking continent, mga 30% ng lupa sa mundo. Kasama ang Pilipinas dito.
hintTl: Ito ang continent kung nasaan ang Pilipinas.

text: What is the boiling point of water at sea level?
explanation: Water boils at 100°C at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure.

text: February 25 is commemorated in the Philippines as the anniversary of which event?
explanation: February 25 marks the 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution, which ended the Marcos regime and installed Corazon Aquino as President.
hint: Think of 1986 and a peaceful uprising along a highway in Metro Manila.
whyB: Independence was proclaimed in Kawit on June 12, 1898.
whyC: Bataan fell on April 9, 1942, now Araw ng Kagitingan.
whyD: The Cry of Pugad Lawin happened in August 1896.
explanationTl: Ang February 25 ay anniversary ng 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution, na nagpatalsik sa Marcos regime at naglagay kay Corazon Aquino bilang President.
hintTl: Isipin mo ang 1986 at ang mapayapang pag-aalsa sa isang highway sa Metro Manila.

text: What is the smallest country in the world by land area?
explanation: Vatican City is the smallest country, with an area of about 44 hectares.

text: Who discovered penicillin?
explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928, leading to modern antibiotics.
hint: He was a Scottish scientist who noticed mold killing bacteria in a petri dish.
whyB: Marie Curie is known for research on radioactivity (radium and polonium).
whyC: Louis Pasteur developed pasteurization and early vaccines, not penicillin.
whyD: Jonas Salk developed the polio vaccine.
explanationTl: Si Alexander Fleming ang naka-discover ng penicillin noong 1928, at ito ang naging simula ng modern antibiotics.
hintTl: Scottish scientist siya na nakapansin na pinapatay ng amag ang bacteria sa petri dish.

text: What is the capital of Australia?
explanation: Canberra is the capital city of Australia, chosen as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.
hint: The capital is a planned city built because two rival big cities could not agree which should be capital.
whyA: Sydney is Australia's largest city, not its capital.
whyB: Melbourne was the temporary seat of government (1901-1927) but is not the capital.
whyD: Brisbane is the capital of Queensland state, not of Australia.
explanationTl: Canberra ang capital ng Australia. Planned city ito na pinili bilang compromise sa pagitan ng Sydney at Melbourne.
hintTl: Hindi ito yung pinakamalaking city; ginawa ito bilang compromise ng dalawang malaking city.

text: Which planet is known as the Red Planet?
explanation: Mars is called the Red Planet due to its reddish appearance from iron oxide (rust).

text: What is the national fruit of the Philippines?
explanation: The mango is the national fruit of the Philippines, known for its sweet varieties.

text: Which year did the Philippines gain independence from the United States?
explanation: The United States recognized Philippine independence on July 4, 1946 through the Treaty of Manila; June 12, 1898 was the declaration of independence from Spain.
hint: It happened the year after World War II ended.
whyB: 1898 is when independence from Spain was declared in Kawit, Cavite, not when the U.S. granted independence.
whyC: 1935 is when the Commonwealth was inaugurated, a transition period before independence.
whyD: 1965 has no link to independence; it is the year Ferdinand Marcos was first elected president.
explanationTl: Noong July 4, 1946, kinilala ng United States ang independence ng Pilipinas sa Treaty of Manila. Yung 1898 naman ay declaration of independence mula sa Spain.
hintTl: Nangyari ito isang taon pagkatapos ng World War II.

text: What is the chemical formula for water?
explanation: The chemical formula for water is H2O, representing two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

text: Which country is known for the Great Wall?
explanation: The Great Wall of China is a historic fortification built to protect Chinese states.

text: Counting both hot and cold deserts, which is the largest desert in the world?
explanation: A desert is defined by very low precipitation, not heat. By that measure the Antarctic Desert (about 14 million sq km) is the largest; the Sahara is the largest hot desert.
hint: A desert is about lack of rain, not about high temperature.
whyA: The Sahara is the largest HOT desert, but it is smaller than the Antarctic.
whyB: The Gobi is a large cold desert in Asia, far smaller than the Antarctic.
whyD: The Kalahari in southern Africa is much smaller.
explanationTl: Ang desert ay base sa sobrang konting ulan, hindi sa init. Kaya ang Antarctic Desert (mga 14 million sq km) ang pinakamalaki; ang Sahara ang pinakamalaking hot desert.
hintTl: Ang desert ay tungkol sa kakulangan ng ulan, hindi sa init.

text: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa, a famous Renaissance artwork.

text: What is the currency of the United Kingdom?
explanation: The Pound Sterling is the official currency of the United Kingdom.

text: Which inert gas is most commonly used to fill incandescent light bulbs to prevent the filament from oxidizing?
explanation: Argon is the gas most commonly used to fill incandescent bulbs because it is inert, cheap and plentiful (about 1% of air), so it keeps the hot tungsten filament from reacting with oxygen.
hint: It is the most abundant noble gas in Earth's air.
whyA: Helium is inert but conducts heat away too fast and is not the usual bulb fill.
whyC: Neon is known for glowing signs, not for filling ordinary incandescent bulbs.
whyD: Hydrogen is not inert; it is flammable and is not used as a bulb fill.
explanationTl: Argon ang karaniwang nilalagay sa incandescent bulb kasi inert ito, mura at marami sa hangin (mga 1%), kaya hindi nag-o-oxidize ang filament.
hintTl: Ito ang pinakamaraming noble gas sa hangin natin.

text: What is the capital of France?
explanation: Paris is the capital of France, home of the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.
hint: It hosted the 2024 Summer Olympics.
whyA: Lyon is a major city known for its cuisine, not the capital.
whyB: Marseille is France's main port city, not the capital.
whyD: Nice is a resort city on the French Riviera.
explanationTl: Ang Paris ang capital ng France, kung nasaan ang Eiffel Tower at ang Louvre.
hintTl: Dito ginanap ang 2024 Summer Olympics.

text: Which Philippine hero is known as the 'Sublime Paralytic'?
explanation: Apolinario Mabini, despite being paralyzed, was a key intellectual in the Philippine Revolution.

text: What is the smallest planet in our solar system?
explanation: Mercury is the smallest planet in our solar system; Pluto is no longer classified as a planet.

text: Which continent is known as the 'Dark Continent'?
explanation: Africa was historically called the 'Dark Continent' due to its unexplored interior.

text: What is the primary source of vitamin D for humans?
explanation: Sunlight triggers vitamin D synthesis in the skin, the primary source for most people.

text: Kapeng barako is a strong coffee traditionally associated with which Philippine province?
explanation: Kapeng barako, from the Liberica coffee species, is traditionally associated with Batangas, especially Lipa City.
hint: Think of the Southern Tagalog province also famous for lomi and balisong.
whyA: Benguet grows highland Arabica coffee, not the traditional barako.
whyC: Bukidnon is a Mindanao coffee producer, but barako is identified with a Southern Tagalog province.
whyD: Davao del Sur is known for Mount Apo Arabica, not barako.
explanationTl: Ang kapeng barako, na Liberica coffee, ay tradisyonal na kilala sa Batangas, lalo na sa Lipa City.
hintTl: Isipin ang probinsya sa Southern Tagalog na sikat din sa lomi at balisong.

text: What is the chemical symbol for iron?
explanation: The chemical symbol for iron is Fe, from its Latin name, ferrum.

text: Which Philippine city is known as the 'City of Pines'?
explanation: Baguio is called the 'City of Pines' because of its cool highland climate and the Benguet pine trees that cover its hills.
hint: It is the cool mountain city that also serves as the Summer Capital of the Philippines.
whyA: Davao is known as the home of the durian and Mount Apo, not pine forests.
whyC: Cebu is known as the 'Queen City of the South'.
whyD: Manila is the national capital, a lowland city without pine forests.
explanationTl: Baguio ang 'City of Pines' dahil malamig doon at puno ng pine trees ang mga bundok.
hintTl: Ito rin ang tinatawag na Summer Capital ng Pilipinas.

text: What is the capital of Canada?
explanation: Ottawa is the capital city of Canada, housing the Parliament of Canada.

text: Who invented the telephone?
explanation: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone in 1876.
hint: He received the first U.S. patent for the telephone in 1876.
whyA: Thomas Edison is known for the phonograph and a practical light bulb, not the telephone.
whyC: Nikola Tesla is known for alternating current (AC) systems.
whyD: Guglielmo Marconi is known for radio (wireless telegraphy).
explanationTl: Si Alexander Graham Bell ang kinikilalang imbentor ng telephone; nakuha niya ang patent noong 1876.
hintTl: Siya ang nakakuha ng unang U.S. patent para sa telephone noong 1876.

text: Which river flows through Egypt?
explanation: The Nile River flows through Egypt, vital for its agriculture and history.

text: What is the national language of the Philippines?
explanation: Filipino, based on Tagalog, is the national language of the Philippines.

text: Which planet is closest to the Sun?
explanation: Mercury is the closest planet to the Sun, orbiting at about 58 million kilometers.

text: What is the currency of Russia?
explanation: The ruble is the official currency of Russia.
hint: Its name starts with the letter R, like the country.
whyB: The euro is used by many European Union members, but Russia is not one of them.
whyC: The dollar is used by the United States and several other countries, not Russia.
whyD: The yen is the currency of Japan.
explanationTl: Ruble ang official currency ng Russia.
hintTl: Nagsisimula rin sa letrang R ang pangalan nito, gaya ng bansa.

text: Which gas is essential for photosynthesis?
explanation: In photosynthesis, plants use carbon dioxide and water, with energy from sunlight, to make glucose and release oxygen.
hint: Plants take in the gas that humans breathe out.
whyA: Oxygen is a product released by photosynthesis, not the gas taken in to make food.
whyC: Plants cannot use nitrogen gas from the air for photosynthesis.
whyD: Hydrogen gas is not taken in during photosynthesis; plants get hydrogen from water.
explanationTl: Sa photosynthesis, gumagamit ang halaman ng carbon dioxide at tubig, kasama ang sikat ng araw, para gumawa ng glucose. Oxygen ang inilalabas nito.
hintTl: Ito ang gas na inilalabas natin kapag humihinga tayo.

text: What is the largest mammal in the world?
explanation: The Blue Whale is the largest mammal, growing up to 100 meters in length.

text: Which country is known for the Taj Mahal?
explanation: The Taj Mahal, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in Agra, India.

text: What is the freezing point of water at sea level?
explanation: Water freezes at 0°C at sea level under standard atmospheric pressure.

text: Boracay Island, famous for its white sand beaches, is part of which province?
explanation: Boracay Island belongs to the municipality of Malay in the province of Aklan, Western Visayas, off the northwest tip of Panay.
hint: It is the Panay province also known for the Ati-Atihan festival in Kalibo.
whyB: Antique is a neighbouring Panay province on the west coast, but Boracay is not part of it.
whyC: Capiz is another Panay province, known as the seafood capital, not Boracay's province.
whyD: Palawan is famous for El Nido and Coron beaches, not Boracay.
explanationTl: Ang Boracay ay nasa bayan ng Malay, sa probinsya ng Aklan, Western Visayas, sa northwest tip ng Panay.
hintTl: Ito yung probinsya sa Panay na sikat din sa Ati-Atihan festival sa Kalibo.

text: Who developed the theory of evolution by natural selection?
explanation: Charles Darwin published the theory of evolution by natural selection in 'On the Origin of Species.'

text: What is the capital of South Africa?
explanation: Pretoria is one of South Africa’s three capital cities, serving as the administrative capital.

text: Which element is the second most abundant in the universe?
explanation: Helium is the second most abundant element in the universe, after hydrogen.
hint: The two lightest elements are also the two most abundant in the universe.
whyA: Hydrogen is the MOST abundant element, not the second.
whyC: Oxygen is the third most abundant in the universe and the most abundant in Earth's crust.
whyD: Carbon is common in living things but far less abundant than helium in the universe.
explanationTl: Helium ang second most abundant element sa universe, kasunod ng hydrogen na number one.
hintTl: Yung dalawang pinakamagaang element ay sila ring pinakamarami sa universe.

text: What is the national sport of the Philippines?
explanation: Republic Act No. 9850 (2009) declared Arnis the national martial art and sport of the Philippines.
hint: It is a Filipino martial art that uses sticks.
whyA: Basketball is the most popular sport but is not the legally declared national sport.
whyC: Volleyball is popular but has no national-sport status.
whyD: Boxing has produced Filipino champions but is not the national sport.
explanationTl: Ang Republic Act No. 9850 (2009) ang nag-declare na Arnis ang national martial art at sport ng Pilipinas.
hintTl: Filipino martial art ito na gumagamit ng stick.

text: Which country is the largest by land area?
explanation: Russia is the largest country by land area, covering about 17.1 million square kilometers.

text: What is the chemical symbol for oxygen?
explanation: The chemical symbol for oxygen is O on the periodic table.

text: Which monument is a symbol of freedom in the United States?
explanation: The Statue of Liberty in New York Harbor, a gift from France dedicated in 1886, is a world-famous symbol of freedom and democracy.
hint: It is a giant statue of a woman holding a torch.
whyA: The Lincoln Memorial honors President Abraham Lincoln.
whyC: The Washington Monument honors George Washington, the first U.S. president.
whyD: Mount Rushmore is a mountain carving of four U.S. presidents' faces.
explanationTl: Ang Statue of Liberty sa New York ay regalo ng France na itinayo noong 1886. Kilala ito sa buong mundo bilang simbolo ng kalayaan.
hintTl: Malaking estatwa ito ng babaeng may hawak na sulo (torch).

text: What is the longest mountain range in the world?
explanation: The Andes, stretching along South America, is the longest mountain range at about 7,000 km.

text: Which Philippine festival is known as the 'Festival of Festivals'?
explanation: Ati-Atihan in Kalibo, Aklan, is called the 'Festival of Festivals' for its vibrant celebration.

text: What is the capital of India?
explanation: New Delhi is the capital city of India, serving as the seat of government.

text: Who was the first man to walk on the moon?
explanation: Neil Armstrong became the first person to walk on the Moon on July 20, 1969, during NASA's Apollo 11 mission.
hint: He was the commander of Apollo 11.
whyA: Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon second, after Armstrong.
whyC: Yuri Gagarin was the first human in space (1961) but never went to the Moon.
whyD: John Glenn was the first American to orbit Earth, not to walk on the Moon.
explanationTl: Si Neil Armstrong ang first na tao na naglakad sa Moon noong July 20, 1969, sa Apollo 11 mission.
hintTl: Siya ang commander ng Apollo 11.

text: Which gas gives soda its fizz?
explanation: Carbon Dioxide is dissolved in soda, creating bubbles and fizz.

text: What is the national tree of the Philippines?
explanation: The Narra tree is the national tree of the Philippines, symbolizing strength and durability.

text: Which country is known as the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes'?
explanation: Finland is called the 'Land of a Thousand Lakes' due to its numerous lakes.

text: What is the chemical symbol for silver?
explanation: The chemical symbol for silver is Ag, from its Latin name, argentum.

text: Which ocean borders the eastern coast of the United States?
explanation: The Atlantic Ocean borders the eastern coast of the United States.

text: Who composed the music of the Philippine national anthem?
explanation: Julian Felipe composed the music of the national anthem in 1898; the original Spanish lyrics came later from Jose Palma's poem 'Filipinas'.
hint: He was a composer from Cavite, commissioned by Aguinaldo.
whyA: Jose Palma wrote the original Spanish lyrics, not the music.
whyC: Claro M. Recto was a statesman and writer, not the anthem's composer.
whyD: Lope K. Santos was a writer and Tagalog grammarian.
explanationTl: Si Julian Felipe ang nag-compose ng music ng national anthem noong 1898; ang Spanish lyrics ay galing sa tula ni Jose Palma na 'Filipinas'.
hintTl: Composer siya galing Cavite, inutusan ni Aguinaldo.

text: What is the largest island in the Philippines?
explanation: Luzon is the largest island of the Philippines (about 109,000 sq km), followed by Mindanao.
hint: It is the island where Metro Manila is.
whyB: Mindanao is the second-largest island.
whyC: Samar is the third-largest island, much smaller than Luzon.
whyD: Palawan is long but far smaller than Luzon.
explanationTl: Ang Luzon ang pinakamalaking island sa Pilipinas (mga 109,000 sq km), sunod ang Mindanao.
hintTl: Dito nakalagay ang Metro Manila.

text: Which scientist proposed the heliocentric model of the solar system?
explanation: Nicolaus Copernicus proposed that the Earth and planets revolve around the Sun.

text: What is the currency of South Korea?
explanation: The South Korean won (KRW) is the official currency of South Korea.
hint: North Korea's currency has the same name.
whyA: The yen is Japan's currency.
whyC: The yuan (renminbi) is China's currency.
whyD: The ringgit is Malaysia's currency.
explanationTl: Ang South Korean won (KRW) ang official currency ng South Korea.
hintTl: Pareho ang pangalan ng currency ng North Korea.

text: Which gas is used in balloons to make them float?
explanation: Helium, being lighter than air, is used to make balloons float.

text: What is the capital of Egypt?
explanation: Cairo, on the Nile River, is the capital of Egypt. The Giza pyramids are just outside the city.
hint: It is the largest city on the Nile River.
whyB: Alexandria is Egypt's major Mediterranean port city, not the capital.
whyC: Giza is the site of the Great Pyramids, next to the capital but not the capital itself.
whyD: Luxor is famous for ancient temples but is not the capital.
explanationTl: Cairo ang capital ng Egypt, nasa tabi ng Nile River. Malapit dito ang mga pyramid sa Giza.
hintTl: Ito ang pinakamalaking lungsod sa tabi ng Nile River.

text: Which Filipino hero is known as the 'Brains of the Katipunan'?
explanation: Emilio Jacinto is called the 'Brains of the Katipunan'; he wrote the Kartilya ng Katipunan and edited its newspaper, Kalayaan.
hint: He wrote the Kartilya, the Katipunan's code of conduct.
whyB: Bonifacio is the Father of the Katipunan and its Supremo, not its 'Brains'.
whyC: Mabini is the 'Brains of the Revolution', adviser to Aguinaldo.
whyD: Del Pilar was a Propaganda Movement leader and editor of La Solidaridad.
explanationTl: Si Emilio Jacinto ang tinatawag na 'Brains of the Katipunan'; siya ang sumulat ng Kartilya ng Katipunan at editor ng Kalayaan newspaper.
hintTl: Siya ang sumulat ng Kartilya, ang code of conduct ng Katipunan.

text: Which planet has the most moons?
explanation: Saturn has the most confirmed moons, over 80 with official names.

text: What is the deepest ocean trench in the world?
explanation: The Mariana Trench is the deepest ocean trench, reaching about 11,000 meters.

text: What is the primary source of energy for hydropower?
explanation: Hydropower uses the energy of moving water to generate electricity.

text: Which country is famous for its pyramids?
explanation: Egypt is renowned for its ancient pyramids, such as those at Giza.

text: What is the chemical symbol for carbon?
explanation: The chemical symbol for carbon is C on the periodic table.

text: Which Philippine city is known as the 'Queen City of the South'?
explanation: Cebu City is called the 'Queen City of the South'; it is the country's oldest city and the trade center of the Visayas.
hint: It is where Magellan planted a cross in 1521.
whyA: Manila is the national capital, not the 'Queen City of the South'.
whyC: Davao is a major Mindanao city but does not carry this title.
whyD: Baguio is the 'Summer Capital of the Philippines'.
explanationTl: Ang Cebu City ang 'Queen City of the South'; siya ang pinakamatandang city sa bansa at trade center ng Visayas.
hintTl: Dito itinanim ni Magellan ang krus noong 1521.

text: What is the capital of Germany?
explanation: Berlin is the capital of Germany; it became the capital of reunified Germany in 1990.
hint: This city was once divided by a famous wall.
whyA: Munich is the capital of Bavaria, not of Germany.
whyC: Hamburg is Germany's largest port city.
whyD: Frankfurt is Germany's financial center, not its capital.
explanationTl: Ang Berlin ang capital ng Germany; naging capital siya ng reunified Germany noong 1990.
hintTl: Dati itong hinati ng isang sikat na wall.

text: Who discovered the theory of gravity?
explanation: Isaac Newton formulated the laws of gravity in the late 17th century.

text: Which river is the longest in South America?
explanation: The Amazon River is the longest in South America, approximately 6,575 km.

text: What is the national dance of the Philippines?
explanation: Tinikling, a bamboo dance, is considered the national dance of the Philippines.

text: Which planet is best known for its large, bright ring system?
explanation: Saturn has the largest and brightest ring system in the solar system, made mostly of ice and rock particles.
hint: It is the sixth planet from the Sun.
whyA: Mars has no ring system; it is known as the Red Planet.
whyC: Venus has no rings; it is known as the hottest planet.
whyD: Mercury has no rings; it is the planet closest to the Sun.
explanationTl: Si Saturn ang may pinakamalaki at pinakamaliwanag na rings sa solar system, gawa sa yelo at bato.
hintTl: Ito ang ika-anim na planeta mula sa Araw.

text: What is the currency of Brazil?
explanation: The Real is the official currency of Brazil.

text: Which gas is the second most abundant in Earth’s atmosphere?
explanation: Oxygen makes up about 21% of Earth’s atmosphere, second to nitrogen.

text: The Burj Khalifa, opened in 2010, is located in which city?
explanation: The Burj Khalifa stands in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It opened in January 2010 at about 828 meters tall.
hint: It is the UAE city known for its palm-shaped man-made islands.
whyB: Abu Dhabi is the UAE capital, but the tower is in Dubai.
whyC: Doha is the capital of Qatar.
whyD: Riyadh is the capital of Saudi Arabia.
explanationTl: Nasa Dubai, United Arab Emirates, ang Burj Khalifa. Binuksan ito noong January 2010, mga 828 meters ang taas.
hintTl: UAE city ito na kilala sa palm-shaped na man-made islands.

text: Which country is known for the Eiffel Tower?
explanation: The Eiffel Tower stands in Paris, France; it was built for the 1889 World's Fair.
hint: Same country whose capital is Paris.
whyA: Italy is known for the Leaning Tower of Pisa.
whyC: Spain is known for the Sagrada Familia.
whyD: Germany is known for the Brandenburg Gate.
explanationTl: Nasa Paris, France ang Eiffel Tower; ginawa ito para sa 1889 World's Fair.
hintTl: Parehong bansa na ang capital ay Paris.

text: What is the chemical symbol for sodium?
explanation: The chemical symbol for sodium is Na, from its Latin name, natrium.

text: Which Philippine province is known for its rice terraces?
explanation: Ifugao is home to the Banaue terraces and other Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
hint: The terraces are in the Cordillera mountains of northern Luzon.
whyB: Pampanga lies on the flat central plains and is known for food and lanterns.
whyC: Batangas is known for Taal Volcano and coffee.
whyD: Quezon is known for coconuts and the Pahiyas Festival.
explanationTl: Nasa Ifugao ang Banaue at iba pang Rice Terraces of the Philippine Cordilleras, isang UNESCO World Heritage Site.
hintTl: Nasa Cordillera mountains sa northern Luzon ito.

text: Who was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize?
explanation: Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1903 and Chemistry in 1911.

text: What is the capital of Thailand?
explanation: Bangkok is the capital and largest city of Thailand.
hint: It is the city where the Grand Palace stands.
whyB: Chiang Mai is a major city in northern Thailand, not the capital.
whyC: Phuket is a resort island in southern Thailand.
whyD: Pattaya is a beach resort city, not the capital.
explanationTl: Bangkok ang capital ng Thailand at ito rin ang pinakamalaking city nila.
hintTl: Dito makikita ang Grand Palace.

text: Which gas is responsible for the greenhouse effect?
explanation: Carbon Dioxide is a primary greenhouse gas, trapping heat in Earth’s atmosphere.

text: What is the national bird of the United States?
explanation: The Bald Eagle is the national emblem and bird of the United States.

text: The International Rice Research Institute (IRRI) is headquartered in which Philippine town?
optionB: Science City of Muñoz, Nueva Ecija
explanation: IRRI, founded in 1960, has its headquarters in Los Baños, Laguna, beside the University of the Philippines Los Baños.
hint: It sits next to a University of the Philippines campus known for agriculture.
whyB: Muñoz, Nueva Ecija hosts PhilRice (Philippine Rice Research Institute), not IRRI.
whyC: Banaue is famous for its rice terraces, not a research institute.
whyD: Tagaytay is a tourist city, not IRRI's home.
explanationTl: Ang IRRI, itinatag noong 1960, ay naka-headquarter sa Los Baños, Laguna, katabi ng UP Los Baños.
hintTl: Katabi ito ng UP campus na kilala sa agriculture.

text: What is the chemical symbol for hydrogen?
explanation: The chemical symbol for hydrogen is H on the periodic table.

text: Which Philippine festival celebrates the Santo Niño?
explanation: The Sinulog Festival of Cebu City, held every third Sunday of January, honors the Santo Niño (Child Jesus) with its signature forward-and-back dance step.
hint: This festival is held in the province where Magellan's Cross is found.
whyB: Panagbenga of Baguio is a flower festival.
whyC: Kadayawan of Davao is a thanksgiving festival for the harvest.
whyD: MassKara of Bacolod is known for its smiling masks, not a Santo Niño feast.
explanationTl: Ang Sinulog Festival sa Cebu City, tuwing ikatlong Linggo ng Enero, ay para sa Santo Niño. Kilala ito sa sayaw na pasulong-paatras.
hintTl: Ginaganap ito sa lugar kung nasaan ang Magellan's Cross.

text: What is the largest continent by land area?
explanation: Asia is the largest continent, covering about 44.58 million square kilometers.

text: Who is credited with developing the first commercially practical incandescent light bulb?
explanation: Thomas Edison developed a long-lasting, commercially practical incandescent light bulb in 1879. Earlier inventors made experimental bulbs, but Edison's design was the first practical for everyday use.
hint: This American inventor also founded the company that became General Electric.
whyB: Nikola Tesla is known for alternating current (AC) systems, not the incandescent bulb.
whyC: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with the telephone.
whyD: Guglielmo Marconi is known for radio (wireless telegraphy).
explanationTl: Si Thomas Edison ang gumawa ng unang praktikal at pangmatagalang incandescent light bulb noong 1879. May mga naunang experimental na bombilya, pero kay Edison ang unang pwedeng gamitin araw-araw.
hintTl: Amerikanong imbentor ito na nagtatag din ng kompanyang naging General Electric.

text: What is the capital of Italy?
explanation: Rome is the capital of Italy and home of landmarks such as the Colosseum.
hint: The Colosseum is found in this city.
whyA: Milan is Italy's financial and fashion center, but not its capital.
whyC: Venice is famous for its canals, but it is not the capital.
whyD: Florence is known for Renaissance art, but it is not the capital.
explanationTl: Rome ang capital ng Italy, kung saan makikita ang Colosseum.
hintTl: Nandito ang Colosseum.

text: Which scientist discovered radioactivity?
explanation: Henri Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896 while studying uranium salts; Marie and Pierre Curie later expanded the research.
hint: The SI unit of radioactivity is named after him.
whyA: Marie Curie coined the term 'radioactivity' and found polonium and radium, but after Becquerel's discovery.
whyB: Rutherford later classified alpha and beta radiation; he did not discover radioactivity.
whyD: Planck is known for quantum theory, not radioactivity.
explanationTl: Si Henri Becquerel ang naka-discover ng radioactivity noong 1896 gamit ang uranium salts; sina Marie at Pierre Curie ang nagtuloy ng research.
hintTl: Ipinangalan sa kanya ang SI unit ng radioactivity.

text: Which river flows through Paris?
explanation: The Seine River flows through Paris, dividing the city into northern and southern halves.

text: What is the national costume of the Philippines for women?
explanation: Baro’t Saya is the traditional national costume for women in the Philippines.

text: Which planet is known as the 'Morning Star'?
explanation: Venus, the brightest planet in our sky, is called the 'Morning Star' when it appears in the east before sunrise (and the 'Evening Star' after sunset).
hint: It is the brightest object in the night sky after the Moon.
whyA: Mercury is seen near sunrise too, but it is much fainter and rarely noticed.
whyC: Mars is called the Red Planet, not the Morning Star.
whyD: Jupiter is bright but is not given the Morning Star name.
explanationTl: Ang Venus, pinakamaliwanag na planet sa langit, ay tinatawag na 'Morning Star' kapag lumalabas siya sa silangan bago sumikat ang araw (at 'Evening Star' pagkalubog nito).
hintTl: Ito ang pinakamaliwanag sa gabi kasunod ng Moon.

text: What is the currency of Mexico?
explanation: The Peso is the official currency of Mexico.

text: Which gas is used in neon signs?
explanation: Neon gas glows bright reddish-orange when electricity passes through it, which is why such lights are called neon signs.
hint: The sign is named after the gas.
whyA: Helium gives a faint pinkish glow and is mostly used in balloons.
whyC: Argon is used in some signs and light bulbs, but the classic sign gas is neon.
whyD: Krypton is used in some lamps, not in typical neon signs.
explanationTl: Ang neon gas ay nagli-glow ng reddish-orange kapag dinaanan ng kuryente, kaya tinawag silang neon signs.
hintTl: Ipinangalan ang sign sa gas mismo.

text: What is the smallest continent by land area?
explanation: Australia is the smallest continent, covering about 7.7 million square kilometers.

text: Who wrote 'Romeo and Juliet'?
explanation: William Shakespeare wrote the tragic play 'Romeo and Juliet' in the 1590s.

text: Which Philippine city is known as the 'Walled City'?
explanation: Manila’s Intramuros is known as the 'Walled City' due to its historic fortified walls.

text: What is the chemical symbol for potassium?
explanation: The chemical symbol for potassium is K, from its Latin name, kalium.

text: Which country is known for the Leaning Tower of Pisa?
explanation: The Leaning Tower of Pisa is located in Pisa, Italy.

text: What is the primary source of energy for wind power?
explanation: Wind power harnesses the kinetic energy of wind to generate electricity.

text: Which Philippine hero is known as the 'National Hero'?
explanation: Jose Rizal is recognized as the National Hero of the Philippines for his writings and martyrdom.

text: Which planet is known as the 'Gas Giant'?
explanation: Jupiter is a gas giant, composed mostly of hydrogen and helium.

text: What is the currency of India?
explanation: The Rupee is the official currency of India.

text: Recreational scuba tanks are most commonly filled with:
explanation: Recreational scuba tanks are usually filled with compressed, filtered air, which is about 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. Pure oxygen becomes toxic under pressure at depth.
hint: Divers breathe basically the same mix of gases we breathe on land, only squeezed into a tank.
whyA: Pure oxygen becomes toxic under the pressure found at diving depths.
whyB: Helium is only mixed into special gases for very deep technical dives; pure helium cannot sustain life.
whyD: Carbon dioxide is a waste gas we exhale; breathing it would be dangerous.
explanationTl: Karaniwang compressed air ang laman ng scuba tank, mga 78% nitrogen at 21% oxygen. Delikado ang pure oxygen kapag malalim na ang dive dahil nagiging toxic ito.
hintTl: Halos pareho lang ito ng hangin na nilalanghap natin sa lupa, pero naka-compress sa tank.

text: What is the capital of Russia?
explanation: Moscow is the capital city of Russia, home to the Kremlin.

text: Which Philippine island is known for its Chocolate Hills?
explanation: The Chocolate Hills are found in Bohol: more than a thousand cone-shaped hills that turn brown in the dry season.
hint: This Visayan island is also home of the tarsier.
whyB: Palawan is known for the Puerto Princesa Underground River, not the Chocolate Hills.
whyC: Luzon has famous sights like the Banaue Rice Terraces, but not the Chocolate Hills.
whyD: Mindanao is known for Mount Apo, not the Chocolate Hills.
explanationTl: Nasa Bohol ang Chocolate Hills: mahigit isang libong burol na nagiging kulay brown tuwing tag-init.
hintTl: Ito rin ang isla sa Visayas na tahanan ng tarsier.

text: Who developed the periodic table?
explanation: Dmitri Mendeleev created the first widely recognized periodic table in 1869.

text: What is the capital of Spain?
explanation: Madrid is the capital city of Spain, known for its cultural heritage.

text: Who discovered America in 1492?
explanation: Christopher Columbus reached the Americas in 1492, initiating European exploration.

text: Which river is the longest in Europe?
explanation: The Volga River is the longest in Europe, stretching about 3,690 km.

text: What is the national emblem of the Philippines?
explanation: The Three Stars and a Sun is part of the Philippine flag, the national emblem.

text: Which planet is known as the 'Blue Planet'?
explanation: Earth is called the 'Blue Planet' due to its abundant water, visible from space.

text: What is the currency of Germany?
explanation: Germany uses the euro. Euro notes and coins replaced the Deutsche Mark in 2002.
hint: Germany belongs to the group of European countries that share one currency.
whyA: The Deutsche Mark was Germany's former currency, replaced by the euro.
whyC: The franc was the former currency of France; Switzerland still uses the Swiss franc.
whyD: The pound is the currency of the United Kingdom.
explanationTl: Euro ang gamit ng Germany. Pinalitan ng euro notes at coins ang Deutsche Mark noong 2002.
hintTl: Kasama ang Germany sa mga bansang European na iisa ang currency.

text: Which gas is used in fire extinguishers?
explanation: Carbon Dioxide is commonly used in fire extinguishers to smother flames.

text: What is the largest country in South America by land area?
explanation: Brazil is the largest country in South America, about 8.5 million square kilometers, nearly half of the continent.
hint: It is the South American country where Portuguese is spoken.
whyA: Argentina is the second-largest country in South America.
whyC: Chile is long and narrow, much smaller than Brazil.
whyD: Peru is smaller than both Brazil and Argentina.
explanationTl: Brazil ang pinakamalaking bansa sa South America, mga 8.5 million square kilometers, halos kalahati ng continent.
hintTl: Ito ang bansa sa South America na Portuguese ang salita.

text: Who painted 'The Starry Night'?
explanation: Vincent van Gogh painted 'The Starry Night' in 1889, a famous post-impressionist work.

text: Siargao Island, known as the 'Surfing Capital of the Philippines', is part of which province?
explanation: Siargao Island, home of the Cloud 9 surf break, is part of the province of Surigao del Norte in the Caraga Region.
hint: Its province shares the 'Surigao' name and lies at the northern tip of Mindanao.
whyA: Surigao del Sur is a neighbouring province on the east coast of Mindanao, but Siargao is not part of it.
whyB: Dinagat Islands is a separate island province in Caraga, north of Siargao, not Siargao's province.
whyD: Agusan del Norte is a Caraga province on the Mindanao mainland, not Siargao's province.
explanationTl: Ang Siargao, kung saan nandoon ang Cloud 9 surf break, ay part ng Surigao del Norte sa Caraga Region.
hintTl: Ang probinsya nito ay may 'Surigao' sa pangalan at nasa northern tip ng Mindanao.

text: What is the chemical symbol for calcium?
explanation: Calcium's chemical symbol is Ca, from the first two letters of its name; its atomic number is 20.
hint: The symbol uses the first two letters of the element's name.
whyB: Cl is chlorine.
whyC: C is carbon.
whyD: Cu is copper, from the Latin 'cuprum'.
explanationTl: Ang chemical symbol ng calcium ay Ca, galing sa unang dalawang letra ng pangalan niya; atomic number 20.
hintTl: Unang dalawang letra ng pangalan ang gamit.

text: Which country is known for the Colosseum?
explanation: The Colosseum, an ancient amphitheater, is located in Rome, Italy.

text: What is the primary source of energy for solar power?
explanation: Solar power harnesses energy from the Sun using photovoltaic cells.

text: Which Philippine hero wrote 'El Filibusterismo'?
explanation: Jose Rizal wrote 'El Filibusterismo,' a sequel to 'Noli Me Tangere.'

text: Which planet is known for its Great Red Spot?
explanation: Jupiter’s Great Red Spot is a massive storm, visible for centuries.

text: What is the currency of Canada?
explanation: The Canadian Dollar is the official currency of Canada.

text: Which gas is the main component of natural gas?
explanation: Methane is the primary component of natural gas, used as a fuel source.

text: What is the capital of Argentina?
explanation: Buenos Aires is the capital and largest city of Argentina.
hint: Its name is Spanish for 'good airs'.
whyB: Córdoba is Argentina's second-largest city, not the capital.
whyC: Mendoza is known for its wine region, not as the capital.
whyD: Rosario is a major port city but not the capital.
explanationTl: Ang Buenos Aires ang capital at pinakamalaking city ng Argentina.
hintTl: Ang ibig sabihin ng pangalan ay 'good airs' sa Spanish.

text: Which Philippine festival is known for its flower floats?
explanation: Panagbenga, Baguio City's flower festival held every February, is known for its flower-covered floats.
hint: It is held in the Summer Capital of the Philippines.
whyB: Sinulog is Cebu's Santo Niño festival, known for street dancing.
whyC: Dinagyang is Iloilo's Santo Niño festival with warrior-style dancing.
whyD: MassKara is Bacolod's festival of smiling masks.
explanationTl: Ang Panagbenga, flower festival ng Baguio tuwing February, ay sikat sa mga float na puno ng bulaklak.
hintTl: Ginaganap ito sa Summer Capital ng Pilipinas.

text: Who proposed the laws of planetary motion?
explanation: Johannes Kepler formulated the three laws of planetary motion in the early 17th century.

text: What is the capital of South Korea?
explanation: Seoul is the capital and largest city of South Korea.
hint: It hosted the 1988 Summer Olympics.
whyB: Busan is South Korea's second-largest city and main port.
whyC: Incheon is known for the main international airport.
whyD: Daegu is a large inland city, not the capital.
explanationTl: Ang Seoul ang capital at pinakamalaking city ng South Korea.
hintTl: Dito ginanap ang 1988 Summer Olympics.

text: Who was the first person to orbit Earth?
explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space and the first to orbit Earth, aboard Vostok 1 on April 12, 1961.
hint: He was a Soviet cosmonaut, not an American astronaut.
whyA: Armstrong was the first to walk on the Moon (1969), not the first to orbit Earth.
whyC: John Glenn was the first AMERICAN to orbit Earth, in 1962, after Gagarin.
whyD: Aldrin was the second man on the Moon.
explanationTl: Si Yuri Gagarin, Soviet cosmonaut, ang first na tao sa space at first na nag-orbit sa Earth sakay ng Vostok 1 noong April 12, 1961.
hintTl: Soviet cosmonaut siya, hindi American astronaut.

text: Which river is the longest in Asia?
explanation: The Yangtze River is the longest in Asia, approximately 6,300 km.
hint: This river flows entirely within China and passes the Three Gorges Dam.
whyB: The Yellow River (Huang He) is China's second-longest river, shorter than the Yangtze.
whyC: The Mekong is long (about 4,900 km) but shorter than the Yangtze.
whyD: The Ganges is about 2,500 km, far shorter than the Yangtze.
explanationTl: Ang Yangtze River sa China ang pinakamahabang ilog sa Asia, mga 6,300 km.
hintTl: Nasa China lang ito at dito makikita ang Three Gorges Dam.

text: What is the national costume of the Philippines for men?
explanation: Barong Tagalog is the traditional national costume for men in the Philippines.

text: Counting outward from the Sun, which planet is third?
explanation: The order from the Sun is Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, so Earth is the third planet.
hint: Recall the order: My Very Educated Mother...
whyA: Venus is second from the Sun.
whyC: Mars is fourth from the Sun.
whyD: Mercury is first, the closest to the Sun.
explanationTl: Ang order mula sa Sun: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars. Kaya Earth ang pangatlo.
hintTl: Alalahanin ang order: My Very Educated Mother...

text: What is the currency of France?
explanation: The Euro is the official currency of France, adopted in 2002.

text: Which gas is used in refrigeration systems?
explanation: Freon, a brand of refrigerants, is commonly used in refrigeration systems.

text: What is the largest country in Africa by land area?
explanation: Algeria is the largest country in Africa, covering about 2.38 million square kilometers.

text: Who wrote 'Pride and Prejudice'?
explanation: Jane Austen wrote 'Pride and Prejudice,' published in 1813.

text: Which Philippine city is known as the 'City of Smiles'?
explanation: Bacolod is called the 'City of Smiles' due to its MassKara Festival.

text: What is the chemical symbol for nitrogen?
explanation: Nitrogen's chemical symbol is N, a single capital letter, because the element name begins with N and no other element took that letter.
hint: Some elements use just the first letter of their name.
whyB: Ni is nickel.
whyC: Na is sodium (from Latin natrium).
whyD: Ne is neon.
explanationTl: N ang symbol ng nitrogen. Isang letter lang, yung first letter ng pangalan niya.
hintTl: May mga element na first letter lang ng pangalan ang symbol.

text: Which country is known for Machu Picchu?
explanation: Machu Picchu, an ancient Incan city, is located in Peru.

text: What is the primary source of energy for geothermal power?
explanation: Geothermal power uses heat from Earth’s interior to generate electricity.

text: Which Philippine hero is known as the 'Great Plebeian'?
explanation: Andres Bonifacio is called the 'Great Plebeian' for his leadership in the Katipunan.

text: Which planet is known for its blue color?
explanation: Neptune looks deep blue because methane in its atmosphere absorbs red light and reflects blue.
hint: It is the eighth planet, named after the Roman god of the sea.
whyA: Mars is known as the Red Planet.
whyB: Jupiter shows tan, brown and white bands and the Great Red Spot.
whyD: Venus looks yellowish-white because of thick sulfuric acid clouds.
explanationTl: Blue ang Neptune kasi ang methane sa atmosphere niya ay nag-a-absorb ng red light at nagre-reflect ng blue.
hintTl: Pang-walong planet ito, ipinangalan sa Roman god ng dagat.

text: What is the currency of Australia?
explanation: Australia uses the Australian dollar as its official currency.
hint: It shares its name with the currency of the United States.
whyB: The pound is the currency of the United Kingdom.
whyC: The euro is used by European Union members, not Australia.
whyD: The yen is the currency of Japan.
explanationTl: Australian dollar ang official currency ng Australia.
hintTl: Kapareho ng pangalan ng currency ng United States.

text: Which gas is used in welding?
explanation: Acetylene is commonly used in welding due to its high flame temperature.

text: What is the capital of Nigeria?
explanation: Abuja is the capital city of Nigeria, planned and built in the 1980s.

text: Which Philippine festival is known for its mask-themed parades?
explanation: The MassKara Festival of Bacolod City is famous for its smiling masks; its name combines 'mass' (many people) and 'cara' (face).
hint: The festival's name sounds like the English word for a face covering.
whyA: Sinulog of Cebu is a dance festival honoring the Santo Niño.
whyC: Panagbenga of Baguio is the flower festival.
whyD: Dinagyang of Iloilo features warrior-style tribal dances honoring the Santo Niño.
explanationTl: Ang MassKara Festival ng Bacolod City ay sikat sa mga nakangiting maskara. Galing ang pangalan sa 'mass' (maraming tao) at 'cara' (mukha).
hintTl: Parang 'mask' ang tunog ng pangalan ng festival.

text: Identify the synonym of 'eloquent'.
explanation: Eloquent means expressing oneself readily, clearly, and effectively, which is synonymous with articulate, while the other options do not match this meaning.

text: Would you like coffee __________ tea?
explanation: The word 'or' is used to present alternatives, making it the correct choice for offering a choice between coffee and tea.

text: I like swimming, ______ my sister likes dancing.
explanation: The word 'but' is used to show contrast between the speaker's preference and their sister's preference.

text: The antonym of 'happy' is:
explanation: Happy means feeling or showing pleasure, and its opposite is sad, meaning unhappy or sorrowful.

text: Choose the correct spelling:
explanation: The correct spelling is 'receive', following the rule 'i before e except after c'.

text: Complete the analogy: Book is to reading as fork is to:
explanation: A book is a tool for reading, just as a fork is a tool for eating.

text: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
explanation: With a third-person singular subject like 'he', the simple present verb takes -s: 'He goes to school.'
hint: Check whether each verb form can stand alone with 'he'.
whyA: 'Go' needs an -s with 'he': 'goes'.
whyC: 'Going' needs a helping verb: 'He is going.'
whyD: 'Gone' is a past participle and needs 'has': 'He has gone.'
explanationTl: Kapag third-person singular ang subject gaya ng 'he', may -s ang verb sa simple present: 'He goes to school.'
hintTl: Tingnan kung kaya bang tumayo mag-isa ng bawat verb form kasama ang 'he'.

text:
Many Catholics fast on Good Friday.

In this sentence, what does 'fast' mean?
explanation: Here 'fast' is a verb meaning to go without food, as many Catholics do on Good Friday.
hint: 'Fast' has several meanings; use the Good Friday context.
whyA: 'Quick' is the adjective meaning of fast, which does not fit 'Catholics fast'.
whyC: 'Hold fast' means hold firmly, but that use needs 'hold' and doesn't fit here.
whyD: Praying is part of Good Friday, but 'fast' itself is about not eating.
explanationTl: Dito, verb ang 'fast' at ang ibig sabihin ay hindi kumain o mag-ayuno, gaya ng ginagawa ng maraming Catholic tuwing Good Friday.
hintTl: Maraming meaning ang 'fast'; gamitin ang context ng Good Friday.

text: Rearrange: The / quick / brown / fox
explanation: The standard English order is article-adjective-adjective-noun, forming 'The quick brown fox'.

text: Which of the following sentences contains an error in subject-verb agreement?
optionA: The list of requirements is on the table.
optionB: Each of the applicants has a valid ID.
optionC: Neither the manager nor the employees is happy with the decision.
explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Employees' is plural, so it should be 'are happy', not 'is happy'.
hint: With 'neither...nor', look at the subject closest to the verb.
whyA: The subject is 'list' (singular), so 'is' is correct; 'of requirements' does not change it.
whyB: 'Each' is singular, so 'has' is correct.
whyD: Sentence C has an error, so 'No error' is wrong.
explanationTl: Sa 'neither...nor', sa subject na pinakamalapit sa verb ito nag-a-agree. Plural ang 'employees', kaya dapat 'are happy', hindi 'is happy'.
hintTl: Sa 'neither...nor', tingnan ang subject na pinakamalapit sa verb.

text: Choose the correct synonym for 'append.'
explanation: Append means to add something as an attachment, so 'add' is the synonym.

text:
Which part of the sentence contains an error?

'The chef cooked the meal quick.'
explanation: 'Quick' is an adjective, but here it describes how the chef cooked, so it must be the adverb 'quickly': 'The chef cooked the meal quickly.'
hint: Ask what the last word is describing: a noun, or the action?
whyA: 'The' is a correct article before 'chef'.
whyB: 'Cooked' is the correct past tense verb.
whyD: There is an error: the word describing the verb needs an adverb form.
explanationTl: Ang 'quick' ay adjective, pero dito dine-describe niya kung paano nagluto yung chef, kaya dapat adverb: 'quickly'.
hintTl: Tanungin mo, ano ba dine-describe ng huling word? Noun ba o yung action?

text: Rearrange the following sentences to form a coherent paragraph: (1) However, it requires dedication. (2) Studying for exams is essential. (3) In summary, consistent effort pays off. (4) First, create a schedule.
explanation: The logical order is introduction (2), step (4), challenge (1), conclusion (3).

text: What is the antonym of 'opaque'?
explanation: Opaque means not transparent, so the opposite is clear or transparent.
hint: Picture a frosted bathroom window versus ordinary window glass.
whyA: Cloudy glass blocks light too, so it is closer to opaque.
whyC: Thick things usually let less light through; that is near opaque, not the opposite.
whyD: Dense material blocks light, which matches opaque rather than opposing it.
explanationTl: Ang opaque ay hindi tinatagusan ng liwanag, hindi mo makita yung nasa likod. Ang kabaligtaran niya ay clear o transparent, parang ordinaryong salamin.
hintTl: Isipin mo yung frosted na bintana sa CR vs. yung malinaw na salamin.

text: Identify the misspelled word in the sentence: 'The committee will accomodate all requests.'
explanation: The correct spelling is 'accommodate', with double 'm' and 'd'.

text: Choose the correct word usage: 'The effect of the new policy _____ immediate.'
explanation: 'Effect' is singular, so it takes 'was' in past tense for subject-verb agreement.

text: Which sentence demonstrates parallelism?
optionA: She likes to swim, running, and to hike.
optionB: She likes swimming, running, and hiking.
optionC: She likes swim, run, and hiking.
optionD: She likes to swim, run, and hiking.
explanation: Parallelism requires consistent grammatical structure, here all gerunds: swimming, running, hiking.

text: What is the contextual meaning of 'query' in 'Please query the database for updates'?
explanation: In computing, 'query' means to request or question the database for information.

text:
Every Christian's path is beset by peril.

In this sentence, 'beset' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Beset' means surrounded or attacked from all sides, so 'surrounded' is the synonym.

text:
The power failure at 8 P.M. caused consternation among the barangay's residents.

In this sentence, 'consternation' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Consternation' means amazement or dismay that hinders or throws into confusion.

text:
The consensus among the congressmen was that the bill would not be passed.

In this sentence, 'consensus' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Consensus' means general agreement or collective opinion.

text:
Tempestuous times preceded the EDSA People Power Revolution.

In this sentence, 'tempestuous' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Tempestuous' means stormy or turbulent, implying emotionally charged.

text:
Imelda Marcos was known for her ostentatious extravagance.

In this sentence, 'ostentatious' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Ostentatious' means characterized by vulgar or pretentious display, so 'showy' is the synonym.

text:
Some believe that the treatment for modern-day depression is complete abstinence from social media use.

In this sentence, 'abstinence' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Abstinence' means the practice of abstaining or avoiding something.

text:
Mary Grace Cafe is a favorite rendezvous for all the titas of Manila.

In this sentence, 'rendezvous' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Rendezvous' means a place appointed for assembling or meeting.

text:
Lola Mona Lisa is so old that her health has regressed to the point that she may die any time soon.

In this sentence, 'regressed' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Regressed' means returned to a former or less developed state, so 'deteriorated' fits.

text:
The garrulous taxi driver annoyed most of his passengers especially the introverted ones.

In this sentence, 'garrulous' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Garrulous' means excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.

text:
A less scrupulous plumber could easily have unnecessarily replaced the drainpipes and run up the cost.

In this sentence, 'scrupulous' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Scrupulous' means diligent, thorough, and extremely attentive to details, so 'careful' is the synonym.

text: Identify the synonym of 'meticulous'.
explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, which is synonymous with precise.
hint: A meticulous worker checks every small detail.
whyA: Careless is the opposite of meticulous.
whyC: Hasty means rushed, which is the opposite of taking careful time.
whyD: Sloppy means messy and careless, the opposite of meticulous.
explanationTl: Ang meticulous ay sobrang maingat at detalyado sa trabaho, kaya kasingkahulugan niya ang precise.
hintTl: Ang meticulous na empleyado ay chine-check ang bawat maliit na detalye.

text: The antonym of 'benevolent' is:
explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kind, so the opposite is malicious or harmful.

text: Fill in the blank: He is afraid _____ flying.
explanation: The preposition 'of' is used with 'afraid' to indicate the object of fear.

text: Which sentence is in passive voice?
optionB: The cat was chased by the dog.
optionD: The dog is chasing the cat.
explanation: In passive voice the subject receives the action and the verb uses a form of 'be' plus a past participle. In 'The cat was chased by the dog,' the cat receives the chasing.
hint: Look for a 'be' verb followed by a past participle, often with 'by' after it.
whyA: The dog does the chasing here, so this is active voice.
whyC: The cat is the doer of 'chases', so this is active voice (and the meaning is reversed).
whyD: 'Is chasing' is present progressive active voice; the dog still does the action.
explanationTl: Sa passive voice, yung subject ang tumatanggap ng action, at may 'be' verb + past participle. Sa 'The cat was chased by the dog,' yung cat ang hinabol.
hintTl: Hanapin mo yung may 'be' verb + past participle, kadalasan may 'by' pa pagkatapos.

text: Identify the error: 'She don't like apples.'
explanation: 'Don't' should be 'doesn't' for third-person singular subject-verb agreement.

text: Complete the analogy: Doctor is to hospital as teacher is to:
explanation: A doctor works in a hospital, just as a teacher works in a school.
hint: The pair links a worker to the PLACE where he or she works.
whyA: A book is a tool a teacher uses, not a workplace.
whyC: A student is the person a teacher serves (like a patient), not a place.
whyD: A pencil is a tool, not the place where a teacher works.
explanationTl: Sa hospital nagtatrabaho ang doctor, kaya sa school naman nagtatrabaho ang teacher. Worker-to-workplace ang relationship.
hintTl: Worker at ang LUGAR kung saan siya nagtatrabaho ang pinagtatapat dito.

text: Choose the correct spelling:
explanation: The correct spelling is 'occurrence', with double 'c' and 'r'.

text: The word 'bank' can mean:
explanation: 'Bank' is a homonym with multiple meanings: edge of a river or a place for money.

text: Rearrange: Is / the / sky / blue
explanation: The standard English order is subject-verb-complement.

text: Which sentence is correct?
optionA: They was going to the market.
optionB: They were going to the market.
optionC: They is going to the market.
optionD: They are going to the market.
explanation: 'They were' is correct for past continuous tense with plural subject.

text: Choose the synonym for 'diligent'.
explanation: Diligent means having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work, synonymous with hardworking.

text: In the sentence 'He ran quick to the store,' the error is:
explanation: 'Quick' should be 'quickly' as an adverb modifying 'ran'.

text: Rearrange the sentences: (1) The dog barked. (2) The thief ran away. (3) The noise woke the owner. (4) The thief entered the house.
explanation: The logical sequence is entry, bark, wake, run away.

text: The antonym of 'abundant' is:
explanation: Abundant means present in great quantity, so the opposite is scarce or rare.

text: Identify the misspelled word: 'The doctor will perscribe medication.'
explanation: The correct spelling is 'prescribe', with 'e' after 'r'.

text: The effect of the drug _____ not known.
explanation: 'Effect' is singular, so it takes 'is' in present tense.
hint: Find the real subject; ignore the phrase that starts with 'of'.
whyA: 'Are' is plural, but the subject 'effect' is singular; 'drug' is only in the 'of' phrase.
whyC: 'Were' is plural, so it does not agree with 'effect'.
whyD: 'Have not known' changes the meaning and does not agree with a singular subject.
explanationTl: Ang subject ay 'effect', singular. Yung 'of the drug' ay prepositional phrase lang, kaya 'is' ang tama.
hintTl: Hanapin mo yung totoong subject. I-ignore mo muna yung phrase na nagsisimula sa 'of'.

text: What is implied by the sentence 'The movie was exciting, but the ending was predictable.'?
optionB: The ending was less exciting than the rest of the movie.
explanation: 'But' sets up a contrast: the movie overall was exciting, while the ending, being predictable, did not keep up that excitement.
hint: What does the word 'but' contrast the ending with?
whyA: Too strong: the sentence calls the movie exciting, so it does not say the movie was bad.
whyC: Contradicts the sentence: a predictable ending is the opposite of a surprising one.
whyD: Overgeneralizes: only the ending is called predictable; the rest was exciting.
explanationTl: Ang 'but' ay nagpapakita ng contrast: exciting ang movie, pero predictable ang ending, kaya hindi kasing-exciting ang ending kumpara sa iba.
hintTl: Ano ang kinokontra ng 'but' sa ending?

text: Which sentence has parallelism?
optionA: He likes to eat, sleep, and watching TV.
optionB: He likes eating, sleeping, and watching TV.
optionC: He likes eat, sleep, and watch TV.
optionD: He likes to eat, to sleep, watch TV.
explanation: All gerunds maintain parallel structure.

text: Contextual meaning of 'bank' in 'I deposited money in the bank':
explanation: In this context, 'bank' refers to a financial institution for money transactions.

text:
President Ronald Drump's efforts to rescind the law were useless.

In this sentence, 'rescind' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Rescind' means to revoke or repeal a law.

text:
The governor has a vindictive attitude toward his ex-wife who cheated on him.

In this sentence, 'vindictive' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Vindictive' means having or showing a strong desire for revenge.

text:
The Spanish colonizers subjugated the native population of the Philippines in order to introduce Christianity.

In this sentence, 'subjugated' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Subjugated' means brought under domination or control.

text:
Paulo wanted to become a doctor because of his desire to mitigate misery in the world.

In this sentence, 'mitigate' most nearly means:
explanation: 'Mitigate' means to make less severe or painful, synonymous with alleviate.

text: Identify the synonym of 'ubiquitous'.
